stories.title: 📜 Gospel of Peter
summaryBullets: The narrative begins with Jesus’ trial, where Pilate washes his hands and refuses responsibility for the sentence.
Herod takes on the role of judge, delivering Jesus to be crucified.
The Jewish leaders and people are portrayed as those pressing for Jesus’ death, intensifying their responsibility.
The text emphasizes Pilate’s innocence and Herod’s central part in condemning Jesus.
Jesus is led out and crucified, silent as though he felt no pain.
The crowd mocks him, taunting, 'Power, save yourself!'
The inscription is placed above the cross: 'This is the King of Israel.'
Jesus’ garments are divided and lots cast among the soldiers.
Joseph requests Jesus’ body and lays it in a tomb.
A great stone is rolled against the entrance.
Soldiers and elders are stationed to guard the tomb.
Seals are set upon the stone to prevent tampering.
A cosmic darkness covers the land at noon, many stumble in fear.
A loud voice is heard from heaven, and the earth shakes.
Two men descend from heaven in shining form and roll away the stone.
The tomb opens, and witnesses see the stone move by itself.
Jesus emerges from the tomb, supported by two heavenly beings, taller than the heavens.
A cross follows them out, and a voice from heaven asks, 'Have you preached to those who sleep?'
The cross answers, 'Yes.'
The guards flee to report what they have seen, and Pilate hears the account with amazement.
crossRefs: Matthew 27:24 — Pilate washes his hands before the crowd.
Luke 23:7–11 — Jesus is sent to Herod for judgment.
John 19:15–16 — The chief priests cry, 'Crucify him!'

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: רָחַץ יָד (raḥaṣ yād) — Greek: νίπτω χεῖρας (níptō cheíras) — Aramaic: שפי ידין (šep̱î yadayin)
translationNotes.note: Ancient gesture symbolizing innocence from guilt; used here to distance Pilate from Jesus’ death.

stories.keyTakeaway: Pilate is depicted as absolving himself of guilt, while Herod and the Jewish leaders assume responsibility for Jesus’ condemnation.
